answer: The three tissue-pair contrasts named in the question — final blood vs baseline blood, dentate gyrus vs baseline blood, and dentate gyrus vs final blood — CANNOT be computed from the supplied capsule: the environment has no R/DESeq2 (no R/Rscript/libR.so/rpy2, no conda/mamba, no apt archives, network unreachable) and the workbook contains no raw integer counts (only the non-integer normalized NormCount matrix). Those three contrasts are also ABSENT from the deposited "DESeq, Comparison 1..9" results, which instead contain nine within-tissue, between-response-group comparisons (C1–C3 = baseline blood, C4–C6 = dentate gyrus, C7–C9 = final blood; each Control-vs-good, Control-vs-bad, bad-vs-good; established via brain-marker baseMean levels, e.g., Snap25 dentate-level ~26–30k on both sides only in C4–C6, and LFC-pattern matching). Under the committed, fixed definition (the data's deposited canonical DEG flag, U/D = padj≤0.05 with the authors' fold-change criterion), the number of unique genes differentially expressed across all nine deposited comparisons is 628. This 628 is NOT presented as the answer to the three named tissue-pair contrasts. Per-comparison canonical DEG counts: C1=22, C2=67, C3=135, C4=115, C5=202, C6=212, C7=119, C8=19, C9=32 (sum 923); auditable alternatives from the same deposited DESeq2 statistics: max-basis DEG union = 844; padj≤0.05 union = 2,244; padj≤0.05 & |log2FC|≥1 union = 443; padj≤0.05 & |log2FC|≥0.5 union = 1,137.
